repos.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
repos.paper_summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is a training algorithm that aligns language models with human preferences using a binary cross-entropy loss, eliminating the need for reinforcement learning. DPO derives this objective by reparameterizing the reward function in standard RLHF as $\hat{r}(x,y) = \beta \log \frac{\pi_\theta(y|x)}{\pi_{\text{ref}}(y|x)}$, where $\pi_\theta$ is the policy being trained and $\pi_{\text{ref}}$ is a fixed reference model. This substitution allows the optimal policy to be extracted in closed form from the Bradley-Terry preference model. The paper proves that under mild assumptions, this reparameterization preserves the full class of representable reward functions without loss of generality. Experiments on IMDb sentiment generation, Reddit TL;DR summarization, and Anthropic dialogue tasks show DPO matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF performance. In sentiment control, DPO achieves higher expected reward at equivalent KL-divergence levels than PPO. For summarization and dialogue, GPT-4 evaluations indicate DPO win rates are comparable to or better than PPO baselines. Limitations include evaluation reliance on GPT-4 judgments and untested scaling beyond 6B parameter models.

repos.title: InteractiveWorld: A Verifiable Human-Centric Environment for Building Better Interactive MLLM Assistants
repos.paper_summary: InteractiveWorld is a simulator built on Isaac Sim for closed-loop interaction between an egocentric MLLM assistant and a human. InteractiveBench is a set of 120 multi-turn tasks in six categories: Guidance, Planning, Accessibility, Decision, Prevention, and Finding. The human is an MLLM agent (Gemini 3.1 Pro in the main experiments) that follows the assistant's guidance and issues one of 36 action primitives. A kinematically driven SMPL+H body performs navigation and manipulation. Success is checked automatically from final object states. Twelve models were evaluated as the assistant. Claude Fable 5.1 passes 41.7% of tasks, and all other models reach at most 33.3%. The best models reach 20.0% on Guidance and 25.0% on Planning, compared with 85.0% on Decision for the best model. With the same human agent, an oracle assistant passes all tasks. Perception and memory errors account for 70.4%–85.7% of first errors across models. The human is simulated by an MLLM rather than real people, and visual input per turn is capped at 32 frames.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Static video benchmarks cannot test whether interactive assistants help people, so the paper proposes a closed-loop simulated environment and benchmark.

digest_headlines.heading: InteractiveWorld
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveWorld models a human who follows assistant guidance, using kinematic body control, collision checks and 36 action primitives.

digest_headlines.heading: InteractiveBench
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveBench has 120 human-reviewed tasks in six categories, scored by final simulator object states rather than answer matching.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: The strongest model, Claude Fable 5.1, passes 41.7% of tasks, and the best models reach only 20.0% on Guidance and 25.0% on Planning.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: InteractiveWorld and InteractiveBench provide a verifiable foundation for developing and evaluating interactive MLLM assistants.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers related work, simulator implementation, benchmark construction and metrics, extra analyses, human-executor validation and future work.

repos.title: Fish Audio S2 Technical Report
repos.paper_summary: Fish Audio S2 is an open-source text-to-speech system that uses a Dual-Autoregressive architecture to generate multi-speaker audio with natural-language control. The model employs a Qwen3-4B backbone for semantic token prediction and a 4-layer network for acoustic detail reconstruction. Training involves a data pipeline that filters audio using a speech quality model and generates rich transcriptions via an ASR model, which are reused as reward signals during Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training. On the Seed-TTS-Eval benchmark, Fish Audio S2 achieves a Word Error Rate of 0.54% in Chinese and 0.99% in English, outperforming CosyVoice 3-1.5B (1.12% and 2.21%, respectively). In production on a single NVIDIA H200 GPU, the system reaches a Real-Time Factor of 0.195 and a time-to-first-audio latency of 100 ms. Evaluation on the Emergent TTS Eval shows an 81.88% win rate against a baseline. A limitation is that performance lags behind MiniMax Speech and ElevenLabs in low-resource languages with under 1,000 hours of training data.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Fine-grained speech control lacks training data at scale, so the report pairs a data pipeline with reinforcement-learning alignment.

digest_headlines.heading: Architecture
digest_headlines.headline: The codec is streaming-capable, and generation splits a slow semantic model from a fast 4-layer acoustic model.

digest_headlines.heading: Data Pipeline
digest_headlines.headline: Three-stage pipeline separates vocals, filters with a speech quality model, and annotates speech with a rich-transcription model, whose outputs also serve as rewards.

digest_headlines.heading: Training
digest_headlines.headline: Training runs in four stages, from a 446-million-parameter tokenizer through over 10 million hours of pre-training to reinforcement-learning post-training.

digest_headlines.heading: Inference Engine
digest_headlines.headline: Streaming inference built on SGLang reaches an RTF of 0.195 and first audio in as little as 100 ms on one high-end accelerator.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Fish Audio S2 reports the lowest error rate on Chinese and English voice-cloning benchmarks and in 11 of 24 languages on the multilingual testset.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The report concludes that its architecture, dual-purpose data pipeline and multi-reward RL support controllable, multi-speaker speech, and that weights and code are released.

digest_headlines.heading: Author
digest_headlines.headline: Core contributors are ranked by contribution, and the other contributors are shuffled with a fixed seed.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix describes the Fish Audio Instruction Benchmark's construction, Gemini 3 Pro judging metrics, and its human-agreement checks.

repos.title: SemMSA: Latent Semantic-Aided Robust Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Incomplete Data
repos.paper_summary: SemMSA is a framework for multimodal sentiment analysis on incomplete MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS data. It adds sentiment-relevant semantic states from a frozen Qwen3-1.7B LLM and aligns language, visual, acoustic, and semantic features with a kernel Gram matrix spectral objective, without an anchor modality. Visual and acoustic features pass through learnable-prompt adapters into the LLM embedding space. The LLM's last hidden state is appended recurrently for 4 steps, producing latent semantic states that are pooled and projected. The Cross-modal Spectral Alignment loss raises the dominant eigenvalue of an RBF kernel Gram matrix over the four normalized representations. A separation regularizer penalizes similarity between instances' dominant directions. Training uses instance-wise Bernoulli masking, and testing sweeps missing rates from 0.0 to 0.9. On MOSI, SemMSA reports Acc-2 of 74.36/73.91 and MAE of 1.011, versus 73.46/72.54 and 1.035 for TF-Mamba. On MOSEI, it reports Acc-2 of 79.61/79.38 and Corr of 0.601, versus 78.83/78.14 and 0.589 for P-RMF. The paper claims a 1.4% average accuracy gain. Limitations: the evaluation uses a single frozen LLM and three seeds, and the paper's SIMS tables are incomplete in the provided text.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Incomplete multimodal sentiment data calls for high-level semantics, which SemMSA supplies from a frozen LLM without decoding text.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior methods reconstruct or fuse missing modalities, or align pairs to an anchor, and the authors say none uses LLM semantics for MSA.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: SemMSA refines frozen-LLM hidden states into latent semantics and aligns all four representations through a kernel Gram matrix's dominant spectral component.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: SemMSA posts the strongest averaged results against all listed baselines under intra-modal missingness on MOSI, MOSEI, and SIMS.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The conclusion restates the two modules and claims effectiveness across SIMS, MOSI, and MOSEI under missing-modality settings.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers the training algorithm, spectral alignment theory, extra results, a case study, limitations, and societal impact.

repos.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversation
repos.paper_summary:
AutoGen is an open-source framework for building LLM applications via multi-agent conversations. The system defines two core concepts: conversable agents, which are customizable entities backed by LLMs, tools, or human inputs, and conversation programming, a method that structures application logic around inter-agent message passing and control flow. Agents use unified interfaces to send messages and generate replies, with an auto-reply mechanism driving the workflow without a central controller. Developers can program interaction patterns using Python code or natural language instructions embedded in agent prompts.

The paper evaluates AutoGen across six domains. On the MATH dataset (5000 problems), the default two-agent configuration achieved 69.48% accuracy, outperforming vanilla GPT-4 at 55.18%. In ALFWorld decision-making tasks, adding a "grounding" agent improved performance by 15% over a ReAct baseline. For coding tasks on OptiGuide, a multi-agent design increased the F-1 score for identifying unsafe code by 8% with GPT-4 and 35% with GPT-3.5-turbo compared to a single-agent setup. The framework reduced the core workflow code for one application from 430 lines to 100 lines. Limitations include the reliance on proprietary models like GPT-4 for peak performance and the lack of formal safety guarantees for fully autonomous agent interactions.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Multi-agent conversation is proposed as the basis for building LLM applications, implemented in the AutoGen framework.

digest_headlines.heading: The AutoGen Framework
digest_headlines.headline: AutoGen rests on conversable agents and conversation programming, where agents exchange messages and control flow emerges from those conversations.

digest_headlines.heading: Applications of AutoGen
digest_headlines.headline: Six example applications test AutoGen across math, retrieval, decision making, coding, group chat and chess.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: The discussion frames AutoGen as a general framework and states that its experiments are early, with safety questions left open.

digest_headlines.heading: Ethics statement
digest_headlines.headline: The ethics statement names privacy, bias, accountability, trust and unintended consequences as risks to address.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers related work with a comparison table, expanded discussion, usage guidelines, future work, and supporting figures.

repos.title: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
repos.paper_summary: HarnessMM reduces repeated reasoning calls in agent harnesses by storing already-resolved actions as executable decision graphs and replaying them when tool feedback satisfies public guards, with recursive self-improvement refining companion harness configurations. A controller sits at the model–tool boundary and keeps model weights fixed. The method reuses stored actions, with literal arguments, causal dependencies and guards, and calls the original actor again when a new semantic decision, unsupported evidence or abstention occurs. On 98 HumanEval tasks, Codex keeps 90.82% success while Tokens/task (k) fall from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54% saving). DeepSeek Harness rises from 71.43% to 85.71% success while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93% saving). On MBPP, the Qwen-backed DeepSeek Harness rises from 90.27% to 91.83% with Tokens/task (k) falling from 53.98 to 10.61. The paper's stated limitations are that savings depend on provider cache and context accounting, that new semantic decisions still require slow reasoning, and that public-state adapters are task specific. Small development sets leave policy-level quality differences uncertain.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Harnesses re-invoke reasoning after each tool result, even when earlier reasoning already fixed the next action.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior methods reduce, route or reuse calls, while HarnessMM targets whether a future reasoning call must recur.

digest_headlines.heading: Problem Formulation
digest_headlines.headline: Substitution saves cost only when removed reasoning tokens exceed the tokens introduced by authorship, routing and fallback.

digest_headlines.heading: HarnessMM: Reusing Decisions
digest_headlines.headline: Guarded reuse executes stored actions only when public guards hold, and otherwise returns control to the original actor.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On 98 HumanEval test tasks, HarnessMM keeps Codex success at 90.82% and raises DeepSeek Harness success to 85.71%.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Savings depend on provider accounting and resolved-action availability, and adapters are task specific.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Stored, guard-checked decisions can replace repeated reasoning calls, and companion studies keep their own scope.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix gives per-iteration MiniWoB++ RSI measurements, development protocols, implementation details and paired-effect definitions.

repos.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
repos.paper_summary: CoworkOS is an agent harness for long-horizon human-agent work. Its three layers are a Main Agent that chooses actions, delegations, and acceptance; a Coordinator Runtime that routes messages and tracks state; and optional Subagents that run in isolated contexts, synchronously or asynchronously. Humans and agents edit the same versioned resources (documents, presentations, CAD models, Blender scenes). A commit rule checks each edit's base revision and returns a conflict for stale edits. Persistent workspaces, semantic memory, and background Jobs with logs let work resume after interruption. The paper reports competitiveness with OpenHands, Codex, and DeepSeek Harness across 12 benchmarks and six application categories, but the text gives no per-benchmark scores for these comparisons. In a post-training case study, CoworkOS ran five rounds on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and the average over eight benchmarks rose from 33.19 to 42.95 (+9.76). Limitations: the study covers one model, the authors state that gains vary across tasks, and the benchmark count is 12 in the abstract but 10 in one figure caption.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: CoworkOS splits task strategy from execution so one agent can handle complex delivery and long-horizon monitoring.

digest_headlines.heading: Preliminaries: Task Formulation and Agency
digest_headlines.headline: Agent tasks are defined by objective, environment, actions, acceptance, and budget, judged along complexity and temporal extent.

digest_headlines.heading: The CoworkOS Agent Harness
digest_headlines.headline: A three-layer harness with synchronous or asynchronous delegation, shared application objects, and durable workspaces and memory.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: CoworkOS ranks among the top two harnesses in every domain average, leading Productivity and ML Coding.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Post-training gains vary across tasks, and the paper concludes that one harness supports productivity, monitoring, and model improvement.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix lists benchmark settings, scoring rules, case inspection protocols, and post-training run records with complete round scores.

repos.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
repos.paper_summary:
Mamba is a sequence model architecture that replaces Transformer attention with selective state space models (SSMs) to achieve linear-time scaling. The method makes SSM parameters $\Delta$, $\mathbf{B}$, and $\mathbf{C}$ functions of the input, allowing the model to selectively propagate or forget information based on content. Because this input-dependency prevents standard convolutional computation, the authors implement a hardware-aware parallel scan algorithm that performs discretization and recurrence in GPU SRAM rather than HBM, using recomputation during backpropagation to limit memory usage.

The architecture combines the SSM layer and MLP into a single block without attention. On language modeling tasks, Mamba-3B outperforms Pythia-3B by 4 points on average common sense reasoning and matches the performance of Pythia-7B. It achieves 5x higher generation throughput than comparable Transformers. For audio and genomics, Mamba reduces FID scores by more than half compared to baselines like Hyena and SaShiMi. The paper notes that evaluation was limited to models below 7B parameters and that the selection mechanism may reduce performance on continuous data modalities where linear time-invariant SSMs excel.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Transformers are costly on long sequences, and Mamba adds input-dependent state space dynamics that scale linearly and match Transformers on language.

digest_headlines.heading: State Space Models
digest_headlines.headline: Structured state space models are linear time-invariant, so their parameters stay fixed across time steps.

digest_headlines.heading: Selective State Space Models
digest_headlines.headline: Selection lets SSM parameters depend on the input, which breaks convolution, so a hardware-aware scan computes the model efficiently.

digest_headlines.heading: Empirical Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: Experiments show Mamba solves synthetic recall tasks and outperforms baselines on language, DNA and audio, with 5× higher throughput.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Selective SSMs trade off on continuous data such as audio, and scaling beyond small sizes remains unassessed.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Mamba is a strong candidate for a general sequence backbone, with selection giving context-dependent reasoning at linear scaling in length.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers selection versus gating, related work, speech-generation training details, and efficiency benchmarks.

repos.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
repos.paper_summary: NorthCUA is a family of computer-use agent models (Nano 9B, Mini 35B, Pro 397B, all built on Qwen3.5), trained through an integrated pipeline that collects and learns from desktop and web GUI experience. The NorthCUA Harness runs tasks in isolated workspaces, records each step, and checks outcomes with task verifiers and an evaluator. The Experience Flywheel builds executable tasks and curates verified trajectories. Staged Learning applies GUI mid-training, supervised fine-tuning on verified long workflows, and joint desktop-web reinforcement learning with GRPO, using verifier outcomes as rewards. Recursive self-improvement reuses tested skills and saved verified milestones on unsolved tasks. The authors report that Pro outperforms Qwen3.8-Max and Kimi-K3 on two grounding benchmarks, OSWorld-Verified, and WebArena-Verified, and that Mini surpasses Kimi-K3 on OSWorld-Verified. NorthCUA-Ultrafast, built on pre-RL Nano with a head that selects finite actions directly, completes matched successful WebArena-Verified tasks 2.3× faster on average than full generation. Stated limitations include unfamiliar software and changing interfaces, verifier coverage, sparse terminal feedback over long workflows, and indirect prompt injection.

digest_headlines.heading: 1Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA couples executable task construction, agent execution, and policy training so experience from software use feeds back into the policy.

digest_headlines.heading: 2Scope and System Overview
digest_headlines.headline: The paper separates single-step control grounding from end-to-end desktop and web tasks, each with fixed requests and completion checks.

digest_headlines.heading: 3NorthCUA Harness: Full-Lifecycle Infrastructure for Computer Use
digest_headlines.headline: The NorthCUA Harness runs each attempt through a shared runtime, long-horizon context management, outcome evaluation, and batch collection with preserved records.

digest_headlines.heading: 4Experience Flywheel: Scaling Grounding and Agentic Experience
digest_headlines.headline: The Experience Flywheel builds grounding examples and executable tasks through three construction routes, and retains progress from hard tasks via skills and milestones.

digest_headlines.heading: 5Staged Learning from Scalable GUI Experience
digest_headlines.headline: Staged Learning trains in three stages: broad GUI mid-training, verified long-horizon supervised fine-tuning, and joint desktop–web reinforcement learning.

digest_headlines.heading: 6Experiments and Analysis
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA-Pro scores 93.3% on ScreenSpot-Pro and 91.0% on OSWorld-G, the highest among systems compared in grounding.

digest_headlines.heading: 7Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA differs from prior systems by integrating decision-time input preservation and complete-attempt weighting with its harness and experience pipeline.

digest_headlines.heading: 8Limitations and Responsible Use
digest_headlines.headline: Open limits include unfamiliar software, verifier coverage, and terminal-only feedback on long workflows.

digest_headlines.heading: 9Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA reports the highest open-source results across three domains and releases its three models and harness code.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists implementation and information boundaries, grounding and task construction details, training data scale, model identities, and extended case studies.

repos.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
repos.paper_summary:
3DCodeVerse is an ecosystem for 3D coding agents with three parts: 3DCodeVerse-2M, a dataset of 2.03 M standalone executable 3D programs with their assets and verification records; a multi-agent harness; and open-model baselines. Programs come from public sources, converted representations (such as DeepCAD sequences translated to CadQuery), and harness-generated code. The harness splits a request into a directed acyclic graph of coding and assembly tasks, executes the output, checks geometry (bounding boxes, contacts, collisions), and has a VLM judge score renders against rubric criteria. Feedback drives repeated revisions without human input.

On 100 text-to-3D object prompts, human evaluators preferred the harness over each model's native harness in 69% to 89% of comparisons. Against Claude Design, both using Claude Opus 5.5, the harness won 90% of human comparisons (Judge Score 88 vs. 37). Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-9B raised the 3DCodeBench execution rate from 0.0% to 84.9%; Qwen3.8-27B rose from 51.9% to 92.9% with SFT and DPO.

Limitations: the object, scene, and graphics comparisons use 100, 50, and 50 prompts; rubric scores come from a VLM judge; and the fine-tuning results use one decoding seed.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: 3DCodeVerse combines a curated executable 3D code dataset with a harness that verifies and revises generated programs.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior 3D code work covers datasets, benchmarks and feedback harnesses, but these remain fragmented across tasks and environments.

digest_headlines.heading: 3DCodeVerse-2M: A large-scale 3D coding dataset
digest_headlines.headline: 3DCodeVerse-2M packages standalone executable 3D programs with assets, captions and separate verification records.

digest_headlines.heading: 3DCodeVerse Harness: A Data Engine for 3D Coding
digest_headlines.headline: The harness uses a multi-agent graph with execution, spatial and visual feedback to revise programs without human input.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Harness outputs win most human comparisons, reaching 90% against Claude Design, and fine-tuning raises execution rates.

digest_headlines.heading: Applications of 3D coding
digest_headlines.headline: Code renders pass a door-and-handle geometry check in 12/12 outputs, versus 7/36 for a frozen video world-action model.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: The authors plan to release datasets, harness, models and training recipes after reporting open-model and harness results.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix details harness runtimes, planning, judge scoring, a recorded run, articulation checks and a video-model comparison.
